subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which tool-result visibility policy should this PR implement for the DeepSeek prefix-cache mitigation: narrow heartbeat/status-only placeholders, existing isolation/pruning/plugin compaction, or broad hard-coded placeholders for tools such as `exec`, `read`, `web`, and `memory`?
rationale: The current patch crosses provider payload and agent reasoning semantics; code inspection can reject the broad knowledge-tool suppression, but the permanent cache policy needs maintainer product intent.

options.title: Narrow result placeholders
options.body: Keep normal tool outputs visible and only summarize formally no-op heartbeat/status results after maintainer-approved semantics and live proof.

options.title: Use existing isolation or compaction
options.body: Prefer heartbeat isolated sessions, context pruning, or Tokenjuice-style compaction for noisy outputs instead of provider-wide hard-coded suppression.

options.title: Accept broad suppression explicitly
options.body: Document and own the behavior that selected tools become invisible to the model, with compatibility tests and live provider proof covering the affected workflows.

recommendation.title: Narrow result placeholders
recommendation.body: Keep normal tool outputs visible and only summarize formally no-op heartbeat/status results after maintainer-approved semantics and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has both official Agents ownership and recent provider/runtime history in the affected area.
